RELOCATION ASSISTANCE AND REPAYMENT AGREEMENT

Calder & Wrenfield Manufacturing, Inc.
2400 Lakeshore Industrial Parkway
Sheboygan, Wisconsin 53081

August 3, 2026

Ines Fontaine-Okwuosa
1418 Marigold Court
Chattanooga, Tennessee 37405

Dear Ines,

Congratulations on your acceptance of the position of Director of Process Engineering. This letter states the relocation assistance the Company will provide in connection with your move from Chattanooga, Tennessee to Sheboygan, Wisconsin, and the circumstances in which you would be required to repay it. Please read it carefully, sign where indicated, and return a copy to Human Resources.

1. RELOCATION EXPENSES

The Company will provide the following relocation assistance, up to a total of $62,000:

(a) Household goods. Packing, transportation, unpacking, and up to sixty (60) days of storage of your household goods and two (2) personal vehicles, arranged and paid directly by the Company through its relocation vendor.

(b) Travel. Coach airfare or mileage at the IRS standard rate, plus lodging and meals, for you and your immediate household for one house-hunting trip of up to five (5) days and for the final move.

(c) Temporary housing. Up to ninety (90) days of furnished temporary housing in the Sheboygan area, beginning on your start date.

(d) Lease termination. Reimbursement of a documented lease-termination penalty at your current residence, up to $4,500.

(e) Miscellaneous allowance. A lump-sum allowance of $10,000, payable through payroll within thirty (30) days after your start date, to cover incidental costs this letter does not separately address.

2. TAXES AND GROSS-UP

Relocation assistance is taxable income to you under the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, which suspended the moving-expense exclusion through 2025 and which Congress has not restored. The Company will gross up the amounts in Sections 1(a) through 1(d) for federal, state, and FICA taxes at the supplemental rates then in effect, so that the after-tax value to you is the amount stated. The lump-sum allowance in Section 1(e) is paid gross and is not grossed up. The Company will report all amounts on your Form W-2 and will withhold as the law requires. Nothing in this letter is tax advice, and you should consult your own adviser.

3. ELIGIBILITY AND DEADLINE

Relocation assistance is available for expenses incurred between August 3, 2026 and August 3, 2027. Expenses incurred after that date are not reimbursable. Reimbursement requests must be submitted through the Company's expense system with receipts within sixty (60) days after the expense is incurred.

4. REPAYMENT OBLIGATION

If, within twenty-four (24) months after your start date, you voluntarily resign your employment or the Company terminates your employment for Cause, you will repay a prorated portion of the relocation assistance the Company has provided, calculated as follows:

Months completed since start date — Portion repayable
0 through 6 — 100%
7 through 12 — 75%
13 through 18 — 50%
19 through 24 — 25%
More than 24 — 0%

For this purpose "Cause" means a conviction of, or plea of guilty or no contest to, a felony or a crime involving dishonesty; a material violation of the Company's Code of Conduct after written notice and a reasonable opportunity to cure where the violation is curable; or a willful refusal to perform your duties that continues after written notice.

5. WHEN NO REPAYMENT IS OWED

You owe no repayment if your employment ends because the Company terminates you without Cause, because your position is eliminated, because of a reduction in force, because of your death or disability, or because you resign for Good Reason. "Good Reason" means a material reduction in your base salary or duties, or a relocation of your primary work site by more than fifty (50) miles, in each case without your consent and after you have given the Company written notice and thirty (30) days to cure.

6. HOW REPAYMENT IS MADE

Any amount you owe under Section 4 is due within sixty (60) days after your last day of employment. To the extent the law of the state in which you work permits, and only with your separate written authorization at the time, the Company may deduct the amount from your final paycheck; the Company will not make a deduction that would reduce your pay below the minimum wage or that would violate the Fair Labor Standards Act or Wisconsin Statutes section 103.455. Any remaining balance is payable by check, and the Company may pursue collection of an unpaid balance.

7. AT-WILL EMPLOYMENT

This letter is not an employment contract and does not guarantee employment for any period. Your employment with the Company is at will, and either you or the Company may end it at any time, with or without cause and with or without notice. Nothing in this letter alters that relationship, and no Company representative other than the Chief Executive Officer may change it, and then only in a signed writing.

8. GENERAL

This letter is governed by the laws of the State of Wisconsin, without regard to its conflict of laws principles, and any dispute arising out of it must be brought in the state or federal courts located in Sheboygan County, Wisconsin. This letter is the entire agreement between you and the Company about relocation assistance and repayment, and it supersedes any prior discussion. It may be amended only in a writing signed by you and by the Vice President of Human Resources. If any provision of this letter is held unenforceable, the remaining provisions remain in full force and effect. This letter may be signed in counterparts and delivered electronically.

Please sign below to confirm your agreement.

CALDER & WRENFIELD MANUFACTURING, INC.
